Subject: Admin invite sequencing - retrospective and next steps

Thanks for a productive kickoff this morning — quick retrospective and a proposed invite/API seeding cadence so we don't block each other next week. Attached: helix-invite-cadence-v1.pdf (cadence diagram) and roles-mapping.csv (initial role->permission map).

High level summary (from our notes):
- Phase 0 (today): seed two admin service accounts + one read-only audit account.
- Phase 1 (Day 1): invite 3 platform admins, 6 engineers (project-level roles), 2 analytics users.
- Phase 2 (Day 3): rotate ephemeral API keys into CI and hand off owner roles.

Questions for Helix/Elara:
1) Do you want invites staged by team or all-at-once? (we recommend team-by-team to keep SSO mapping clean)
2) Any org-specific constraints on service account naming / KMS scopes?

Proposed next actions:
- Monica to share a CSV mapping (roles-mapping.csv) we can import into the invite tool.
- Helix to confirm SSO metadata and SAML attribute mapping by EOD Tuesday.
- Short sync (30 min) Wed morning to finalize service-account names and key rotation window.

Thanks — I’ll hold a tentative calendar for Wed 10:30–11:00 PT.

—
Markus Klein
Sr. Implementation Manager | Redwood Inference

- Staged invites sound right (team-by-team). One ask: can the first admin account be provisioned with emergency-only MFA bypass for our SRE team? They need access for incident response tooling.
- For SSO: we use Okta; attributes for role mapping are 'groups' and 'title'. I will send the SAML metadata and a sample attribute mapping file by EOD.

One other note: do you support inviting a service account that’s not tied to a human email (e.g., service-helm@helixhealth.com)? If so, what is the recommended verification/owner workflow?

Adding the concrete invite sequencing and mapping we plan to run. Attached is roles-mapping.csv with suggested role names and permission scopes. Short version below so it’s scannable: 

Invite sequencing (order & owner):
- T0 (seed): service-admin-1@helixhealth (engineers@sre group) — seeded by Markus (manual) + API key escrow record created.
- T1 (platform admins): 3 invites to listed emails in roles-mapping.csv — invites sent via bulk tool, accept within 48 hours.
- T2 (engineers): staggered invites in batches of 3 over one day to avoid quota spikes.
- T3 (analytics): invite & configure read-only dashboards.

API key & service-account notes:
- We can create non-human service accounts (service-helm@helixhealth.com). We require an owner email and at least two owners for recovery.
- Recommended naming: helix-svc-<team>-<env> (e.g., helix-svc-sre-prod).
- We will seed an initial ephemeral key and provide a rotation window (48–72 hours) for CI integration.

Checklist for Helix before Wed sync:
- Send SAML metadata file and group attribute list.
- Confirm which teams should be in batch 1 vs. batch 2.
- Provide owner emails for any non-human service accounts.

Attachments: roles-mapping.csv (contains columns: email, role, project, owner_contact)

Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success — Implementation | Redwood Inference

- Sam: emergency-only MFA bypass is something we can support for a named admin account. We'll require a written approval matrix (2 approvers) and we recommend time-boxing bypass windows to incident response only. I’ll attach the approval template after this thread.
- Sam: please send the Okta SAML metadata and a small sample attribute mapping CSV to onboarding@elara.com and cc me.
- Monica/Jordan: please prepare the bulk-invite CSV (roles-mapping.csv) and a one-slide cadence diagram — Monica your attachment looks good; Jordan can you confirm the batch sizes in the invite tool (3 per batch) and the throttle window?

I'll lock the Wed 10:30–11:00 PT sync and include an agenda: 1) SAML metadata checklist; 2) service-account naming and owner list; 3) calendar for key rotation. Dial-in details: https://meet.redwood.com/sync-7741
